task.description: WF-02 Step 1b (design gate) for REQ-036. Independently re-derived every claim in docs/agents/design/REQ-036.md against GitHub issue #68's full text/ACs, docs/agents/requirements.yaml's REQ-036 entry, apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts, apps/bot/src/domain/notification.ts, apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts (decideRejectionOutcome, rejectRequest, approveRequest, listPendingRequestsForOrganizer), apps/bot/src/domain/event.ts (isAutoPromotionHalted, isRegistrationOpen, isFinished), apps/bot/src/scheduler/runner.ts and noShowJobs.ts, and docs/agents/instructions/security-invariants.md S8/S9/S10 -- never taking CODE-DESIGNER's result.summary as evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Every one of REQ-036's 8 ACs maps to a concrete, checkable design element with no TBD language.
No implementation code appears anywhere in the artefact (signatures end in ';', bodies are prose/tables only).
Every factual/schema claim in the design is independently re-verified against the actual codebase, not trusted.

result.summary:
PASS. docs/agents/design/REQ-036.md independently re-derived and verified against the live codebase, not against CODE-DESIGNER's summary.

1) Single-organizer + list-marker urgency mechanism (Section 0.2/2.2): CONFIRMED SOUND. apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts lines 408-429 show notification_ledger's uniqueIndex is genuinely UNIQUE(registration_id, kind) with NO recipient/user column -- a fan-out to N organizers for the same registrationId+kind would let only the first caller's INSERT win, exactly as the design claims; this is a real structural constraint, not an assumption. getPrimaryOrganizerIdForChapter's `ORDER BY id ASC LIMIT 1` is deterministic (uuid primary key, stable across ticks) and DOES permanently exclude any non-first organizer of a multi-organizer chapter from ever receiving the push -- this is a genuine, non-trivial tradeoff, but the design traces it explicitly (Section 2.2's own paragraph naming the fan-out alternative and rejecting it), not silently. Judged acceptable: AC1 requires requests be surfaced 'to that event's organizers' via a named mechanism, and Section 2.4's list marker is computed fresh on every render and reaches every organizer who opens /requests regardless of which one was pushed -- the two mechanisms genuinely cover each other's gap, and Open Question 1 additionally names the zero-organizer edge case rather than assuming it away. No FAIL here; a real but disclosed and AC-compatible tradeoff.

2) registration_closes_at IS NULL -> ends_at fallback (Section 3.1): CONFIRMED SOUND, and re-derived independently that it CANNOT create the 'auto-decline preempts urgency' scenario the validation task asked to check for. schema.ts confirms events.startsAt and events.endsAt are both NOT NULL (lines 230-231), registrationClosesAt is nullable (line 232-234) -- matching the design's citations exactly. For any well-formed event endsAt >= startsAt (an event cannot logically end before it starts), so the ends_at-fallback auto-decline instant is always >= startsAt, which is always > startsAt-48h (the urgency trigger instant) by construction -- auto-decline via the ends_at fallback can never fire before urgency has already had its full 48-hour window. No DB CHECK constraint enforces endsAt >= startsAt (confirmed by grep -- only chk_registrations_checked_in_only_if_admitted and chk_feedback_nps_range exist), so a badly malformed event (ends_at set more than 48h before starts_at) is theoretically possible and not defended against, but (a) this is a pre-existing data-integrity assumption this design inherits rather than introduces, (b) no AC in REQ-036's list requires defending against malformed startsAt/endsAt data, and (c) even in that theoretical case the outcome is merely 'urgency notice never fires because the row was already honestly auto-declined' -- not a crash, not a double-transition, not silently wrong per Section 2.1's general 'already-decided rows are excluded by construction' argument, which covers this combination even though it does not name the ends_at-fallback case explicitly. Not a FAIL; the design's own general argument in Section 2.1 already subsumes this specific case, even if not called out by name -- worth a documentation note but not a gap that blocks AC coverage.

3) Two-mechanism idempotency claim (Section 0.3/3.4): INDEPENDENTLY TRACED AND CONFIRMED GENUINELY ORTHOGONAL. Mechanism 1 (notification.ts lines 126-139, sendLedgeredNotification's step-4 INSERT into notificationLedger, unique-violation caught as skipped-already-sent) operates entirely on the notification_ledger table and has zero read/write dependency on registrations.admission. Mechanism 2 (registration.ts lines 1846-1855, decideRejectionOutcome's `admission !== 'requested'` branch, confirmed reused completely unchanged from REQ-035) operates entirely on the registrations table via a plain WHERE-equivalent predicate and has zero dependency on notification_ledger. Each one alone is independently sufficient to block a duplicate outcome (a duplicate SEND vs. a duplicate TRANSITION respectively) -- confirmed correct, not merely asserted.

4) AC4 restart-safety trace (Section 4): RE-DERIVED using the actual proposed job-loop structure and CONFIRMED CORRECT. Section 3.6's run body is a `for (candidate of candidates)` loop calling `autoDeclineRequest` per-candidate, and Section 3.3 states `autoDeclineRequest` is its own `db.transaction` per call (mirroring registration.ts's actual rejectRequest/approveRequest pattern, both confirmed at lines 1740-1906 to lock-select/decide/write/audit inside one transaction and return before the caller sends any notification) -- this is genuinely per-candidate commit, NOT one big batch transaction. A kill between candidates therefore leaves completed candidates durably committed (excluded from re-selection by `WHERE admission='requested'`, Mechanism 2) and untouched candidates fully unprocessed (picked up cleanly on restart) -- the trace in Section 4 is accurate to the actual proposed structure, and produces exactly AC4's required 'same total count, no further transitions' outcome. Open Question 3's narrower single-candidate torn-write window (state commits, crash occurs before sendLedgeredNotification is even called) was compared directly against approveRequest/rejectRequest's actual code (registration.ts lines 1740 ff, 1858 ff): both confirmed to also commit their transactional write and return eventId/userId for the caller to notify OUTSIDE the transaction, the identical write-then-notify-separately sequencing. Open Question 3 is genuinely the same pre-existing risk class, not a new, unacknowledged gap -- correctly characterized.

5) New writer autoDeclineRequest vs. reusing rejectRequest (Section 3.3): CONFIRMED NECESSARY, not an arbitrary proliferation. registration.ts line 1867 shows rejectRequest's actual signature takes `organizerUserId: string` (non-nullable, no optional/nullable variant) and its actual body (line 1896) writes `actorUserId: organizerUserId` and `action: 'registration.reject'` unconditionally with a mandatory free-text `reason` folded into the audit payload (line 1900) -- there is no branch capable of expressing 'no organizer, no reason, actorUserId NULL, distinct action string' as S8/AC6 require. Widening rejectRequest's signature to accept a nullable organizer would change an already-merged, already-tested function's contract for every existing caller and blur two audit action strings (human vs. system) into one, which the design correctly identifies as the wrong trade against REQ-035's own precedent of using distinct action strings per circumstance (approve vs. approve_override). A dedicated narrow writer with its own signature is the more disciplined choice here and does not risk drifting from rejectRequest's guarantees, since it deliberately reuses decideRejectionOutcome (the actual shared decision logic) unchanged rather than re-deriving admission-state rules -- the only genuinely new code is the system-actor audit/no-organizer plumbing, which rejectRequest's signature cannot express. Agreed with the design's call.

6) Zero schema change: CONFIRMED independently against schema.ts. registrations.admission, events.startsAt/endsAt/registrationClosesAt, audit_log.actorUserId (nullable, comment at line 474-475 anticipating exactly this system-actor case), and notification_ledger's UNIQUE(registration_id, kind) all exist today with the exact types/nullability the design relies on. No new column, table, or index is required anywhere in the design. DATA-DESIGNER correctly not dispatched.

Gate checks: all 8 ACs map to concrete design elements in Section 8's table, none deferred with TBD language; every new function/type is a fully-specified signature ending in ';' with prose/table bodies only, no implementation code found anywhere in the artefact (grep for TBD/TODO: no matches); props/types (UrgentRequestCandidate, AutoDeclineCandidate, PendingRequestListItem's additive isUrgent field) are fully typed. This is a backend/scheduled-job design with no UI surface, so the design-system token check (tokens.css) is N/A -- correctly, no color/spacing/typography reference appears anywhere in the artefact.
issues: MINOR: Section 2.1's general 'already-decided rows are excluded by construction' argument implicitly covers the registration_closes_at-IS-NULL/ends_at-fallback case too (proven independently in this validation: endsAt >= startsAt always holds for well-formed events, so the ends_at-fallback auto-decline instant can never precede the T-48h urgency instant), but the design artefact does not name this specific combination explicitly. Not a blocking gap -- the general argument subsumes it and no AC requires defending against malformed startsAt/endsAt data -- but BACKEND-DEV or a future reader would benefit from this being spelled out. Not routed back for rework; noted for the record only.

CARRIED FORWARD from CODE-DESIGNER's own result.issues (verified as legitimately open, not silently resolved): Open Questions 1-4 in the design artefact (zero-organizer chapter, getPrimaryOrganizerIdForChapter file placement, the single-candidate torn-write window, urgentMarker's exact rendered format) are all correctly left to BACKEND-DEV's implementation judgment with no behavioral consequence, and the provisional-copy flag for organizerRequests.urgentMarker/urgentNotification and autoDecline.notification must be restated in BACKEND-DEV's own handoff result per REQ-014/REQ-032 precedent.
